geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the generic bent-bar dominant mass with a split-wing massing that can create a clearer entry gap/public threshold while preserving one dominant compact body.
Use the long axis of the mass to split toward the frontage and define a more legible ground seam.
Introduce a modest separation to create a usable void without fragmenting the overall mass.
Keep the two wings related as one architectural gesture rather than unrelated fragments.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the primary mass logic from a purely courtyard-based seed into a stronger carved response so the street edge can read as an actual public threshold rather than a sealed bulk.
Increase the carved/public void proportion to make the open-space figure legible in plan and section.
Align the void opening with the program access side in frame so the frontage becomes an active ground response.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass across all four views, with a recognizable bent-bar/courtyard-derived silhouette and no obvious view-to-view collisions. The form is reasonably oriented to the parcel, but it underuses the public threshold: the blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly, with no clear carved court, undercut, or entry seam on that side. As a neighborhood-living mass, it is plausible in scale and general typology, but the dominant gesture is still somewhat generic and box-adjacent, with the void logic not yet strong enough to make the street response feel intentional. The section is calm and capacity-bearing enough for early stage, so it passes hard program fit, but it would benefit from a more explicit public ground carve and a cleaner access anchor.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a finished pavilion/restaurant image, so its facade and material language should not be copied; only the massing logic and entry legibility are transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise compact massing with a legible public-facing threshold and a modest attached vertical element; the building reads as one coherent object rather than fragmented pieces.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the visible views.
The road frontage/access edge is not strongly articulated as an active public threshold.
The mass could read as more purposeful if the dominant gesture were tied to a clearer void or entry incision.
